paragraphs.title: Jacob Arrives at the Well and the Flocks

easy.question: Where did Jacob go?
answers: To the land of the people of the east
easy.explanation: The first verse says that Jacob went to the land of the people of the east.

easy.question: What did Jacob see in the field?
easy.explanation: The second verse says, “Behold, a well in the field.”

easy.question: How many flocks of sheep were lying by the well?
easy.explanation: The verse says that three flocks of sheep were there.

medium.question: Why were the flocks watered from that well?
answers: Because the flocks were watered from that well
Because there was no water in the field
medium.explanation: The verse explains that the flocks were watered from that well.

medium.question: In the phrase “three flocks of sheep lying by it,” what does “lying” mean?
medium.explanation: Here, “lying” means resting or reclining near the well.

medium.question: What order of actions is described in the third verse?
answers: They watered the sheep, gathered the flocks, and replaced the stone
They replaced the stone, watered the sheep, and gathered the flocks
They gathered the flocks, rolled away the stone, watered the sheep, and replaced it
medium.explanation: First the flocks were gathered, then the stone was rolled away, the sheep were watered, and the stone was replaced.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the stone being put back over the well after the sheep were watered?
answers: The well was normally covered after use
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that the stone was put back after the sheep were watered, suggesting that this was the usual practice.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the well served more than one flock?
answers: Three flocks were there, and all the flocks gathered at the well
Jacob went to the land of the east
challenge.explanation: The mention of three flocks and the gathering of all the flocks shows that the well served many flocks.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the fact that the stone over the well was large?
answers: The well was on a mountain
Several people may have been needed to roll the stone
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the stone was large, suggesting that moving it required considerable effort.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the stone being put back over the well after the sheep were watered?
answers: The well was normally covered after use
questions.explanation: The verse specifically says that the stone was put back after the sheep were watered, suggesting that this was the usual practice.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the well served more than one flock?
answers: Three flocks were there, and all the flocks gathered at the well
Jacob went to the land of the east
questions.explanation: The mention of three flocks and the gathering of all the flocks shows that the well served many flocks.

questions.question: What can be understood from the fact that the stone over the well was large?
answers: The well was on a mountain
Several people may have been needed to roll the stone
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the stone was large, suggesting that moving it required considerable effort.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Meets Rachel by the Well

easy.question: From which city did the shepherds Jacob met come?
easy.explanation: The shepherds told Jacob, “We are from Haran.”

easy.question: Who was Rachel?
easy.explanation: The verses say that Rachel was Laban’s daughter.

easy.question: What did Jacob do after seeing Rachel and Laban’s sheep?
answers: He rolled away the stone and watered the flock
easy.explanation: Jacob rolled the stone away from the well and watered Laban’s flock.

medium.question: Why did the shepherds say they could not water the sheep immediately?
answers: They were waiting for all the flocks to gather
Rachel had asked them to wait
medium.explanation: They were waiting for all the flocks to gather so that the stone could be rolled away together.

medium.question: In the phrase “it is yet high day,” what does “high day” mean?
answers: The day was still far from over
medium.explanation: Jacob meant that it was still daytime and there was plenty of time to water and feed the sheep.

medium.question: What happened while Jacob was still speaking with the shepherds?
medium.explanation: The verse says, “While he yet spake with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Rachel’s arriving with her father’s sheep?
answers: She was merely visiting her father’s house
She did not know the sheep
She helped care for and tend the flock
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Rachel kept her father’s sheep, showing that she tended them.

challenge.question: What was unusual about Jacob’s action compared with what the shepherds said?
answers: He rolled away by himself a stone the shepherds were waiting to move together
He asked Rachel to move the stone
challenge.explanation: The shepherds said they were waiting to move the stone together, but Jacob rolled it away himself.

challenge.question: Why could Jacob understand that Rachel was his relative before meeting Laban?
answers: The shepherds told him she was Isaac’s daughter
He learned that she was Laban’s daughter, and Laban was his mother’s brother
Rachel told him she was his sister
challenge.explanation: Jacob knew that Laban was his mother’s brother, so Laban’s daughter Rachel was his cousin.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Rachel’s arriving with her father’s sheep?
answers: She was merely visiting her father’s house
She did not know the sheep
She helped care for and tend the flock
questions.explanation: The verse says that Rachel kept her father’s sheep, showing that she tended them.

questions.question: What was unusual about Jacob’s action compared with what the shepherds said?
answers: He rolled away by himself a stone the shepherds were waiting to move together
He asked Rachel to move the stone
questions.explanation: The shepherds said they were waiting to move the stone together, but Jacob rolled it away himself.

questions.question: Why could Jacob understand that Rachel was his relative before meeting Laban?
answers: The shepherds told him she was Isaac’s daughter
He learned that she was Laban’s daughter, and Laban was his mother’s brother
Rachel told him she was his sister
questions.explanation: Jacob knew that Laban was his mother’s brother, so Laban’s daughter Rachel was his cousin.

paragraphs.title: Jacob’s Emotional Meeting with Rachel and Laban

easy.question: Whom did Jacob kiss?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Jacob kissed Rachel.”

easy.question: What did Jacob do after kissing Rachel?
answers: He lifted up his voice and wept
easy.explanation: The verse says that Jacob lifted up his voice and wept.

easy.question: Where did Laban bring Jacob?
easy.explanation: Laban ran to Jacob, embraced him, kissed him, and brought him to his house.

medium.question: Why did Rachel tell her father about Jacob?
answers: Jacob told her that he was her relative
medium.explanation: Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s relative and Rebekah’s son, so she ran to tell Laban.

medium.question: What caused Laban to run to meet Jacob?
answers: The news that Jacob, his sister’s son, had arrived
medium.explanation: When Laban heard about Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet him.

medium.question: In the phrase “Surely thou art my bone and my flesh,” what does “surely” express?
answers: Recognition that Jacob truly was his relative
An order for Jacob to leave
medium.explanation: Laban was affirming that Jacob was genuinely his close relative.

challenge.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: Laban brought Jacob home, and then Jacob met Rachel
Jacob met Rachel, Rachel told Laban, and Laban welcomed Jacob
Rachel told Laban, Jacob wept, and Laban sent him away
challenge.explanation: Jacob first met Rachel and wept; Rachel then told Laban; finally Laban ran to Jacob and brought him home.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Laban’s response to Jacob?
answers: Laban recognized Jacob as family and welcomed him
Laban feared that Jacob would stay with him
challenge.explanation: Laban embraced Jacob, called him his own flesh and blood, and hosted him for a month.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Jacob and Laban did not part immediately after meeting?
answers: Jacob lifted up his voice and wept
Jacob stayed with Laban for a month
challenge.explanation: The passage explicitly says that Jacob stayed with Laban for a month.

questions.question: What order of events is described in these verses?
answers: Laban brought Jacob home, and then Jacob met Rachel
Jacob met Rachel, Rachel told Laban, and Laban welcomed Jacob
Rachel told Laban, Jacob wept, and Laban sent him away
questions.explanation: Jacob first met Rachel and wept; Rachel then told Laban; finally Laban ran to Jacob and brought him home.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Laban’s response to Jacob?
answers: Laban recognized Jacob as family and welcomed him
Laban feared that Jacob would stay with him
questions.explanation: Laban embraced Jacob, called him his own flesh and blood, and hosted him for a month.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Jacob and Laban did not part immediately after meeting?
answers: Jacob lifted up his voice and wept
Jacob stayed with Laban for a month
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly says that Jacob stayed with Laban for a month.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Agrees to Work for Rachel

easy.question: How many daughters did Laban have?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Laban had two daughters.

easy.question: Whom did Jacob love?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Jacob loved Rachel.”

easy.question: How many years did Jacob offer to work for Rachel?
easy.explanation: Jacob said that he would serve Laban seven years for Rachel.

medium.question: Why did Laban ask Jacob what his wages should be?
answers: Jacob was working for him, and Laban wanted to establish the payment
medium.explanation: Laban understood that Jacob was working for him and asked what compensation he wanted.

medium.question: In the phrase “serve me for nought,” what does “for nought” mean?
medium.explanation: “For nought” means without receiving wages or compensation.

medium.question: How did Laban respond to Jacob’s offer to work seven years for Rachel?
answers: He asked Jacob to work for less time
He agreed, saying it was better to give Rachel to Jacob than to another man
medium.explanation: Laban said that Jacob’s offer was preferable and agreed that Jacob should stay with him.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the seven years seeming to Jacob like only a few days?
answers: His love for Rachel made the time seem to pass quickly
The work lasted only a few days
challenge.explanation: The verse directly connects Jacob’s sense of time with his love for Rachel.

challenge.question: Which detail distinguishes Leah from Rachel in the verses?
answers: Leah was the elder, while Rachel was younger and beautiful
Rachel was the elder, while Leah was younger
challenge.explanation: The verses identify Leah as the elder and Rachel as the younger, and describe Rachel as beautiful.

challenge.question: What can be understood from Laban’s words, “It is better that I give her to thee”?
answers: Laban had already decided Jacob must work seven years
Laban preferred Jacob as a husband for Rachel to another man
Laban did not know who Rachel was
challenge.explanation: Laban said he preferred giving Rachel to Jacob rather than to someone else.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the seven years seeming to Jacob like only a few days?
answers: His love for Rachel made the time seem to pass quickly
The work lasted only a few days
questions.explanation: The verse directly connects Jacob’s sense of time with his love for Rachel.

questions.question: Which detail distinguishes Leah from Rachel in the verses?
answers: Leah was the elder, while Rachel was younger and beautiful
Rachel was the elder, while Leah was younger
questions.explanation: The verses identify Leah as the elder and Rachel as the younger, and describe Rachel as beautiful.

questions.question: What can be understood from Laban’s words, “It is better that I give her to thee”?
answers: Laban had already decided Jacob must work seven years
Laban preferred Jacob as a husband for Rachel to another man
Laban did not know who Rachel was
questions.explanation: Laban said he preferred giving Rachel to Jacob rather than to someone else.

paragraphs.title: The Wedding Feast and Laban’s Deception

easy.question: Who asked Laban to bring his wife to him?
easy.explanation: Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife.”

easy.question: What did Laban do after Jacob asked for his wife?
answers: He gathered the people and held a feast
easy.explanation: Laban gathered all the people of the place and made a feast.

easy.question: Whom did Laban bring to Jacob in the evening?
easy.explanation: In the evening, Laban took Leah and brought her to Jacob.

medium.question: Why did Jacob ask Laban to bring his wife to him?
answers: He wanted to hold a feast
His appointed days had been completed
The people of the place requested it
medium.explanation: Jacob said that his days were fulfilled, meaning that the agreed period of service had ended.

medium.question: In the phrase “my days are fulfilled,” what does it mean?
medium.explanation: Jacob believed the agreed period of work was complete and that it was time to receive his wife.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Laban brought Leah, then held a feast, and finally Jacob asked for his wife
Jacob asked for his wife, Laban held a feast, and then brought Leah
Laban held a feast, Jacob left, and then Zilpah was given to Leah
medium.explanation: Jacob first asked for his wife; Laban then held a feast; in the evening he brought Leah.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Laban involved the people of the place in the event?
answers: He gathered all the people and held a feast
challenge.explanation: The text explicitly says that Laban gathered all the people and made a feast.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Jacob’s request for “my wife” followed by Laban’s bringing Leah?
answers: Laban brought his daughter Leah, although Jacob had only said “my wife”
Leah was one of the people of the place
challenge.explanation: Jacob asked for his wife, but the passage says that Laban took Leah and brought her to him.

challenge.question: What does giving Zilpah to Leah show about Zilpah?
answers: She was one of the local women
She was Laban’s maid given to Leah
challenge.explanation: The verse says that Laban gave Leah Zilpah his maid as a handmaid.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Laban involved the people of the place in the event?
answers: He gathered all the people and held a feast
questions.explanation: The text explicitly says that Laban gathered all the people and made a feast.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Jacob’s request for “my wife” followed by Laban’s bringing Leah?
answers: Laban brought his daughter Leah, although Jacob had only said “my wife”
Leah was one of the people of the place
questions.explanation: Jacob asked for his wife, but the passage says that Laban took Leah and brought her to him.

questions.question: What does giving Zilpah to Leah show about Zilpah?
answers: She was one of the local women
She was Laban’s maid given to Leah
questions.explanation: The verse says that Laban gave Leah Zilpah his maid as a handmaid.

paragraphs.title: The Discovery and the New Agreement

easy.question: Whom did Jacob discover in the morning instead of Rachel?
easy.explanation: In the morning Jacob saw that the woman given to him was Leah, not Rachel.

easy.question: For whom did Jacob say he had worked for Laban?
easy.explanation: Jacob said, “Did not I serve with thee for Rachel?”

easy.question: Who explained that the younger daughter was not given before the firstborn?
easy.explanation: Laban said, “It must not be so done in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.”

medium.question: What reason did Laban give for giving Leah to Jacob?
answers: In their country, the younger was not given before the firstborn
Rachel did not want to marry
Jacob had not worked enough years
medium.explanation: Laban claimed that their custom required the elder daughter, Leah, to marry before Rachel.

medium.question: What did Laban ask Jacob to do in order to receive Rachel too?
answers: Complete Leah’s week, then work another seven years
medium.explanation: Laban told Jacob to complete Leah’s bridal week and then work another seven years for Rachel.

medium.question: In the phrase “before the firstborn,” what does “firstborn” refer to here?
medium.explanation: The contrast with “the younger” shows that the firstborn was the older sister, Leah.

challenge.question: What can be understood from Laban’s explanation of marriage customs?
answers: The older sister was customarily given before the younger
People were forbidden to work before marriage
The younger sister always married first
challenge.explanation: Laban presented a local rule that the younger daughter was not given before the older one.

challenge.question: Why did Jacob say, “Wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?”
answers: Laban had not paid his wages
Laban gave him Leah instead of Rachel after Jacob had worked for Rachel
Laban sent him to work elsewhere
challenge.explanation: Jacob expected Rachel after seven years of work, but discovered in the morning that he had received Leah.

challenge.question: How many years of work did Jacob commit to in total for Leah and Rachel?
challenge.explanation: Jacob worked seven years and was required to work another seven years for Rachel, totaling fourteen years.

questions.question: What can be understood from Laban’s explanation of marriage customs?
answers: The older sister was customarily given before the younger
People were forbidden to work before marriage
The younger sister always married first
questions.explanation: Laban presented a local rule that the younger daughter was not given before the older one.

questions.question: Why did Jacob say, “Wherefore then hast thou beguiled me?”
answers: Laban had not paid his wages
Laban gave him Leah instead of Rachel after Jacob had worked for Rachel
Laban sent him to work elsewhere
questions.explanation: Jacob expected Rachel after seven years of work, but discovered in the morning that he had received Leah.

questions.question: How many years of work did Jacob commit to in total for Leah and Rachel?
questions.explanation: Jacob worked seven years and was required to work another seven years for Rachel, totaling fourteen years.

paragraphs.title: Jacob Marries Rachel and Continues Working

easy.question: Whom did Laban give to Jacob as a wife?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Laban gave Rachel to Jacob as a wife.

easy.question: Whom did Laban give to Rachel as a maid?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Laban gave Bilhah to Rachel as her maid.

easy.question: How many more years did Jacob work for Laban?
easy.explanation: The verse says that Jacob served Laban another seven years.

medium.question: What did Jacob do before Laban gave him Rachel?
medium.explanation: Jacob completed the required week, and then Laban gave him Rachel.

medium.question: In this passage, what is a “maid”?
medium.explanation: A maid is a female servant; Bilhah was given to Rachel to serve her.

medium.question: Why did Jacob work another seven years after receiving Rachel?
answers: He loved Rachel and agreed to remain with her
medium.explanation: Jacob loved Rachel, so he agreed to serve Laban for another seven years.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the statement that Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah?
answers: Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly compares Jacob’s love for Rachel and Leah and says that he loved Rachel more.

challenge.question: Who gave Bilhah to Rachel, and what was Bilhah’s role?
answers: Laban gave her to Rachel as a maid
Jacob gave her to Rachel as a sister
Leah gave her to Rachel as a wife
challenge.explanation: Laban gave Bilhah to Rachel, and Bilhah served as her maid.

challenge.question: What does the order of events show about Jacob?
answers: He received Rachel before completing his service
He completed the required period, received Rachel, and then worked another seven years
He worked only seven years and never received Rachel
challenge.explanation: The verses describe Jacob completing the week, receiving Rachel, and then serving another seven years.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the statement that Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah?
answers: Jacob loved Rachel more than Leah
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly compares Jacob’s love for Rachel and Leah and says that he loved Rachel more.

questions.question: Who gave Bilhah to Rachel, and what was Bilhah’s role?
answers: Laban gave her to Rachel as a maid
Jacob gave her to Rachel as a sister
Leah gave her to Rachel as a wife
questions.explanation: Laban gave Bilhah to Rachel, and Bilhah served as her maid.

questions.question: What does the order of events show about Jacob?
answers: He received Rachel before completing his service
He completed the required period, received Rachel, and then worked another seven years
He worked only seven years and never received Rachel
questions.explanation: The verses describe Jacob completing the week, receiving Rachel, and then serving another seven years.

easy.question: Who saw Leah’s situation?
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD saw that Leah was hated.

easy.question: What did the LORD do for Leah?
answers: He sent her to another land
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD opened Leah’s womb.

easy.question: Who was barren according to the verse?
easy.explanation: The end of the verse says that Rachel was barren.

medium.question: What connection does the verse make between Leah’s situation and the LORD’s action?
answers: Because Leah was hated, the LORD opened her womb
Because Leah was not barren, the LORD sent her away
Because Rachel loved Leah, the LORD blessed Rachel
medium.explanation: The verse directly connects Leah’s being hated with the LORD opening her womb.

medium.question: In the phrase “Leah was hated,” what does “hated” mean here?
medium.explanation: Here, “hated” means not loved or favored, describing Leah’s difficult situation.

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Rachel became barren, and then the LORD saw Leah
Leah gave birth, and then Rachel became barren
The LORD saw Leah, opened her womb, and Rachel was barren
medium.explanation: The verse first says that the LORD saw Leah, then opened her womb, and finally mentions Rachel’s barrenness.

challenge.question: What central contrast appears in the verse?
answers: Leah was hated but had her womb opened, while Rachel was loved but barren
Leah and Rachel were equally barren
Leah was loved and Rachel was hated
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts Leah’s lack of love with Rachel’s barrenness.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the LORD seeing Leah’s situation and acting for her?
answers: The verse emphasizes attention to Leah’s distress
challenge.explanation: The focus on Leah’s difficult situation shows that the LORD noticed her distress and helped her.

challenge.question: Which detail creates the comparison between the two women?
answers: The name “LORD” appears at the end
The verse says that Leah’s womb was opened and immediately adds that Rachel was barren
challenge.explanation: Placing the two descriptions together clearly contrasts Leah’s opened womb with Rachel’s barrenness.

questions.question: What central contrast appears in the verse?
answers: Leah was hated but had her womb opened, while Rachel was loved but barren
Leah and Rachel were equally barren
Leah was loved and Rachel was hated
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts Leah’s lack of love with Rachel’s barrenness.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the LORD seeing Leah’s situation and acting for her?
answers: The verse emphasizes attention to Leah’s distress
questions.explanation: The focus on Leah’s difficult situation shows that the LORD noticed her distress and helped her.

questions.question: Which detail creates the comparison between the two women?
answers: The name “LORD” appears at the end
The verse says that Leah’s womb was opened and immediately adds that Rachel was barren
questions.explanation: Placing the two descriptions together clearly contrasts Leah’s opened womb with Rachel’s barrenness.

easy.question: Who gave birth to a son in this verse?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Leah conceived, and bare a son.”

easy.question: What did Leah name her son?
easy.explanation: Leah named her son Reuben.

easy.question: Why did Leah name her son Reuben?
answers: Because the LORD had looked upon her affliction
easy.explanation: Leah said, “Surely the LORD hath looked upon my affliction.”

medium.question: What is the order of events in the verse?
answers: Leah conceived, gave birth, named the child Reuben, and explained the name
Leah named the child, conceived, and then gave birth
Leah gave birth, her husband named the child, and then she conceived
medium.explanation: The verse describes conception, birth, naming, and then Leah’s explanation.

medium.question: In the phrase “looked upon my affliction,” what does “affliction” mean?
medium.explanation: Leah was speaking about her sorrow and difficult situation.

medium.question: Why did Leah say, “Now therefore my husband will love me”?
answers: She had found a new home
She hoped that having a son would make her husband love her
medium.explanation: Leah hoped that the birth of her son would cause her husband to love her.

challenge.question: What verbal connection exists between the name Reuben and Leah’s words?
answers: The name echoes the words “the LORD hath looked”
The name is connected with love
The name is connected only with poverty
challenge.explanation: Reuben’s name echoes Leah’s words, “the LORD hath looked upon my affliction.”

challenge.question: What can be inferred about Leah’s feelings before Reuben’s birth?
answers: She felt that her husband did not love her enough
She feared she would have no home
challenge.explanation: Her hope that her husband would now love her suggests that she had previously felt unloved.

challenge.question: Which statement expresses Leah’s hope rather than merely describing an event?
answers: Leah gave birth to a son
Leah thought that her husband would now love her
challenge.explanation: The birth and naming are events, while her husband’s love was Leah’s hope.

questions.question: What verbal connection exists between the name Reuben and Leah’s words?
answers: The name echoes the words “the LORD hath looked”
The name is connected with love
The name is connected only with poverty
questions.explanation: Reuben’s name echoes Leah’s words, “the LORD hath looked upon my affliction.”

questions.question: What can be inferred about Leah’s feelings before Reuben’s birth?
answers: She felt that her husband did not love her enough
She feared she would have no home
questions.explanation: Her hope that her husband would now love her suggests that she had previously felt unloved.

questions.question: Which statement expresses Leah’s hope rather than merely describing an event?
answers: Leah gave birth to a son
Leah thought that her husband would now love her
questions.explanation: The birth and naming are events, while her husband’s love was Leah’s hope.

easy.question: What did Leah name her son?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “She called his name Simeon.”

easy.question: What did Leah say the LORD had heard?
easy.explanation: Leah said, “The LORD hath heard I was hated.”

easy.question: What did the LORD give Leah according to the verse?
easy.explanation: Leah said that the LORD had given her this son also.

medium.question: Why did Leah name her son Simeon?
answers: Because the LORD heard her distress
Because she wanted a short name
Because it was her father’s name
medium.explanation: The name Simeon is connected with Leah’s statement that the LORD had heard that she was hated.

medium.question: In the phrase “the LORD hath heard I was hated,” what does “hated” mean?
medium.explanation: Leah describes herself as someone who was not loved.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in the verse?
answers: The child was named, then Leah conceived and gave birth
Leah gave birth, named the child, and then conceived
Leah conceived, gave birth, spoke, and named the child
medium.explanation: The verse describes conception, birth, Leah’s words, and finally the naming of Simeon.

challenge.question: What connection exists between Leah’s words and the name Simeon?
answers: The name is connected with the word “heard”
The name is connected with the word “hated”
The name is connected with the word “given”
challenge.explanation: Leah said that the LORD had heard her, and Simeon’s name echoes that idea.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the words “this son also”?
answers: This son was in addition to children already born
The son did not belong to her
challenge.explanation: The word “also” shows that this was another son in addition to the one she already had.

challenge.question: What does the verse explicitly attribute to the LORD hearing Leah?
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically says that the LORD gave her another son; it does not say here that Jacob’s attitude changed.

questions.question: What connection exists between Leah’s words and the name Simeon?
answers: The name is connected with the word “heard”
The name is connected with the word “hated”
The name is connected with the word “given”
questions.explanation: Leah said that the LORD had heard her, and Simeon’s name echoes that idea.

questions.question: What can be understood from the words “this son also”?
answers: This son was in addition to children already born
The son did not belong to her
questions.explanation: The word “also” shows that this was another son in addition to the one she already had.

questions.question: What does the verse explicitly attribute to the LORD hearing Leah?
questions.explanation: The verse specifically says that the LORD gave her another son; it does not say here that Jacob’s attitude changed.

paragraphs.title: The Birth of Levi and the Hope for a Bond

easy.question: What did Leah do before speaking in this verse?
answers: She gave birth to a son
easy.explanation: The verse begins by saying that she conceived and gave birth to a son.

easy.question: What name did Leah give her son?
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Therefore was his name called Levi.”

easy.question: Why did Leah name her son Levi?
answers: He was born on the road
She had borne her husband three sons
easy.explanation: Leah said, “I have born him three sons.”

medium.question: What did Leah hope would happen after the birth of her third son?
answers: Her husband would become attached and draw close to her
She would give birth to a daughter
medium.explanation: Leah said, “Now this time will my husband be joined unto me,” expressing hope that he would draw close to her.

medium.question: In the phrase “my husband be joined unto me,” what does “joined” mean?
answers: Become attached and draw close to her
Rejoice in his son from a distance
medium.explanation: Leah hoped that her husband would become emotionally close to her.

medium.question: How is the birth of three sons connected with the name Levi?
answers: Levi was the last son born
The name expressed Leah’s hope that her husband would become attached to her
medium.explanation: Leah connected having three sons with her hope that her husband would draw close to her.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the word “again” at the beginning of the verse?
answers: Leah had already given birth to sons before this birth
